topics.title: Introduction, Scope & Informal Practices
explain: AS 15 prescribes accounting treatment and disclosures for employee benefits provided by employers, excluding share-based payments.
It covers full-time, part-time, casual staff, directors, and benefits provided to dependents or paid via trusts and insurance companies.
Benefit costs must be matched with the period during which the employee renders service, regardless of cash payment timing.
A contract of service creates an employer-employee relationship, whereas a contract for services is an independent contractor relationship.
Informal practices create a legal or constructive obligation if past history creates a valid expectation with no realistic alternative but to pay.

flow.title: Evaluating Informal Practices & Obligation
steps: Identify informal benefit practice
Review past payment pattern
Assess employee expectations created
Determine if realistic alternative exists
Recognize liability if obligation exists

topics.example: An employer regularly pays an informal festival bonus of ₹10,000 every Diwali based on past custom; this creates a recognized obligation.
remember: Share-based payments (ESOPs) are completely excluded from AS 15.
mistakes: Accounting for informal festival bonuses on a cash basis instead of accruing them during the service period.

quiz.q: Which of the following is EXCLUDED from the scope of AS 15?
quiz.why: AS 15 explicitly excludes employee share-based payments from its accounting scope.

o: An employer-employee relationship with direction and control
An outsourcing contract with no oversight
A contract for rendering technical advisory services
quiz.why: Contract of service creates an employer-employee relationship where work instructions must be obeyed.

topics.title: Applicability & Meaning of Employee
explain: AS 15 became applicable from April 1, 2006 in its entirety for Level 1 enterprises, with relaxations for non-Level 1 entities.
The term 'employee' is not strictly defined in AS 15 but includes full-time, part-time, permanent, casual, temporary staff, and whole-time directors.
A formal employment agreement is not strictly required if the economic substance indicates an employer-employee relationship.
Key indicators of employment include direct supervision, provision of tools and materials, and specified workplace location.
Services provided through an entity with no other clients and no financial risk represent an individual employee relationship in substance.

flow.title: Determining Employee Status Under AS 15
steps: Check if formal contract exists
Assess degree of direction and control
Verify who provides tools and equipment
Check client diversity and financial risk
Classify as employee or independent contractor

topics.example: A software consultant working exclusively at a firm's office using company computers under daily manager supervision is treated as an employee under AS 15.
remember: AS 15 applies fully from April 1, 2006 for Level 1 entities.
mistakes: Assuming temporary or casual workers without a written contract are excluded from AS 15.

quiz.q: AS 15 applies in its entirety from April 1, 2006 primarily to:
quiz.why: AS 15 applies in its entirety to Level 1 enterprises from April 1, 2006.

quiz.q: Which of the following individuals are covered under AS 15?
quiz.why: AS 15 explicitly includes whole-time directors, casual, part-time, and temporary staff as employees.

topics.title: Short-Term Employee Benefits & Compensated Absences
explain: Short-term benefits fall due wholly within 12 months after the end of the period in which related service is rendered.
Categories include regular wages, short-term compensated absences, profit-sharing/bonus plans, and non-monetary benefits.
Short-term benefits are recognized on an undiscounted basis as an expense in the period service is rendered.
Accumulating absences carry forward to future periods, while non-accumulating absences (e.g., maternity leave) expire if unused and are expensed when taken.
Accumulating leave may be vesting (entitled to cash encashment on leaving) or non-vesting (usable in future but no cash encashment on leaving).
Profit-sharing/bonus plans are accrued when a present obligation exists from past events and a reliable estimate can be made via a formula.

flow.title: Accounting for Short-Term Compensated Absences
steps: Check if absence entitlement accumulates
If non-accumulating, expense when taken
If accumulating, estimate unused leave carried forward
Calculate expected additional cost using expected utilization
Accrue undiscounted expense and liability

topics.example: An entity with 100 employees expects 8 employees to take an extra 1.5 days of leave next year from carried-over leave; it accrues 12 days (8 x 1.5) of salary as a liability at year-end.
remember: Short-term employee benefits are always measured on an undiscounted basis.
mistakes: Discounting short-term employee benefit obligations to present value.

quiz.q: Short-term employee benefits are those payable within how many months after the end of the service period?
quiz.why: Short-term benefits fall due wholly within 12 months after the end of the service period.

quiz.q: Non-accumulating compensated absences (such as maternity leave) should be recognized:
o: As a provision estimated using actuarial methods
Evenly spread over the employee's entire service period
As a long-term liability at discounted present value
quiz.why: Non-accumulating absences do not carry forward and are recognized as expense when the absence occurs.

topics.title: Post-Employment Benefits: Defined Contribution vs Defined Benefit Plans
explain: Post-employment benefits include gratuity, pension, provident fund, and post-employment medical care.
In Defined Contribution Plans (DCP), the enterprise pays fixed contributions into a separate fund with no further obligation; actuarial and investment risks fall on the employee.
In Defined Benefit Plans (DBP), the employer promises specific benefit amounts; actuarial and investment risks fall on the employer.
If an employer funds gratuity through an insurance policy (e.g., LIC), it remains a DBP if the employer must pay directly or top up deficits.
Plan assets in a DBP are netted off against the defined benefit obligation on the Balance Sheet, while reimbursement rights are shown separately as asset and liability.

flow.title: Classifying Post-Employment Benefit Plans
steps: Examine benefit plan structure
Check if employer pays fixed contribution into separate fund
Determine who bears actuarial and investment risks
If employee bears risk, classify as Defined Contribution Plan
If employer bears risk, classify as Defined Benefit Plan

topics.example: If an employer contributes 12% of salary to Provident Fund and has no obligation to make up for investment shortfalls, it is a Defined Contribution Plan.
remember: In Defined Contribution Plans, risks fall on the employee; in Defined Benefit Plans, risks fall on the employer.
mistakes: Treating an insured gratuity scheme as a Defined Contribution Plan when the employer remains liable for shortfalls.

quiz.q: Under a Defined Contribution Plan, who bears the investment and actuarial risks?
quiz.why: In Defined Contribution Plans, the employee bears both actuarial and investment risks.

quiz.q: How are plan assets presented in a Defined Benefit Plan Balance Sheet?
o: Shown as an independent income item in P&L
Deducted from defined benefit obligation to present net liability or asset
Always shown as a fixed asset at historical cost
quiz.why: Plan assets are reduced from the defined benefit obligation to disclose the net amount in the Balance Sheet.

topics.title: Accounting Treatment & P&L Components for Defined Benefit Plans
explain: Net Balance Sheet Liability = Present Value of DBO minus Fair Value of Plan Assets minus Unrecognized Past Service Cost.
If the net calculation yields an asset, it is capped at the lower of that net amount OR the present value of economic benefits (refunds/reduced contributions).

P&L expense comprises 7 components: current service cost, interest cost, expected return on assets, actuarial gains/losses, past service cost, curtailment/settlement effects, and asset ceiling adjustments.
A settlement eliminates all further legal/constructive obligations (e.g., lump-sum commuted pension payment).
A curtailment occurs when an enterprise commits to reduce covered employees or cut future plan benefits.

flow.title: Measuring Defined Benefit Liability & P&L Charge
steps: Calculate present value of defined benefit obligation
Deduct fair value of plan assets and unrecognized past service cost
Determine net balance sheet liability (or capped net asset)
Calculate 7 P&L cost components
Recognize net expense in Statement of Profit and Loss

topics.example: A company has a DBO of ₹6,000, plan assets of ₹5,100, unamortized past service cost of ₹180; the net liability on the Balance Sheet is ₹720 (or ₹138 after 10% curtailment adjustment).
remember: Net defined benefit asset recognized in Balance Sheet cannot exceed present value of available refunds or contribution reductions.
mistakes: Forgetting to deduct fair value of plan assets when calculating net defined benefit liability.

quiz.q: When fair value of plan assets exceeds defined benefit obligation, the resulting asset is capped at:
o: Present value of economic benefits from refunds or reduced future contributions
Actuarial loss of the current year
quiz.why: AS 15 limits net asset recognition to the lower of the net amount and present value of refunds/reductions in future contributions.

quiz.q: A curtailment in a defined benefit plan occurs when an employer:
o: Increases pension rates for all retirees
Reduces covered employees or cuts plan benefits
Converts a defined contribution plan to cash
quiz.why: A curtailment happens when an employer reduces covered employees or reduces benefits under the plan.

topics.title: Actuarial Assumptions, Gains, and Losses
explain: Actuarial assumptions must be unbiased, mutually compatible, and reflect the best estimates of post-employment variables.
Demographic assumptions deal with mortality, employee turnover rates, disability, early retirement, and dependent eligibility.
Financial assumptions deal with discount rates (market yields on government bonds), future salary levels, medical costs, and return on assets.
Actuarial gains and losses arise from experience adjustments (difference between past assumptions and actual outcomes) and assumption changes.
AS 15 requires immediate recognition of all actuarial gains and losses in the Statement of Profit and Loss as income or expense.

flow.title: Processing Actuarial Gains and Losses
steps: Set unbiased demographic and financial assumptions
Perform actuarial valuation at balance sheet date
Compare actual outcomes with previous assumptions
Calculate effect of changes in actuarial assumptions
Recognize total actuarial gain/loss immediately in P&L

topics.example: Omega Ltd receives an actuarial valuation revealing a ₹6 lakh pension surplus due to assumption changes; the full ₹6 lakh must be credited to P&L immediately, not spread over future years.
remember: Actuarial gains and losses must be recognized IMMEDIATELY in Profit and Loss.
mistakes: Amortizing actuarial gains or losses over the remaining average service life of employees (which is prohibited under AS 15).

quiz.q: Under AS 15, actuarial gains and losses must be recognized:
o: Over average remaining service life of employees
Immediately in the Statement of Profit and Loss
quiz.why: AS 15 strictly mandates immediate recognition of actuarial gains and losses in Profit and Loss.

quiz.q: Which of the following is classified as a demographic actuarial assumption?
o: Expected rate of return on plan assets
quiz.why: Employee turnover rate is a demographic assumption regarding workforce characteristics.

topics.title: Other Long-Term & Termination Benefits
explain: Other long-term benefits include long-service leave, sabbatical leave, jubilee benefits, long-term disability, and bonuses payable ≥ 12 months after service period.
Measured similarly to defined benefit plans, but all actuarial gains/losses and past service costs are recognized immediately in P&L.
Termination benefits are payable when employment is terminated before normal retirement date or on voluntary redundancy (e.g., VRS).
Recognized as liability and expense only when enterprise has a detailed formal plan approved AND a reliable estimate can be made.
Termination benefits falling due > 12 months after balance sheet date must be discounted using an appropriate discount rate.
If uncertainty exists regarding how many employees will accept voluntary redundancy, a contingent liability is disclosed under AS 29.

flow.title: Recognizing Termination Benefits
steps: Decision or offer made for early termination or VRS
Formulate approved detailed formal plan
Determine if reliable estimate of obligation can be made
If due within 12 months, record undiscounted expense
If due after 12 months, record discounted present value expense

topics.example: A company announces an approved VRS scheme expecting 50 workers to accept within 6 months costing ₹50 lakhs; it records an undiscounted provision of ₹50 lakhs immediately.
remember: Termination benefits require an approved detailed formal plan and a reliable estimate before recognition.
mistakes: Recognizing termination costs based on informal management intentions before an approved formal plan exists.

quiz.q: Termination benefits payable more than 12 months after the balance sheet date must be:
o: Expensed on cash payment date only
Discounted to present value using an appropriate discount rate
Recognized as short-term liabilities on an undiscounted basis
quiz.why: Termination benefits falling due after 12 months must be discounted to present value.

quiz.q: What is required before an enterprise can recognize a provision for termination benefits?
o: Payment of cash to all employees
An approved detailed formal plan and a reliable estimate of the obligation
Approval from the Income Tax department
Completion of 5 years of service by all employees
quiz.why: Recognition requires an approved detailed formal plan and a reliable estimate of the obligation.
